Recent research supports treating sampled ranking as a distinct evaluation condition: negative sampling can distort metric values and reverse model ordering. RecSys 2025 examines sampling resolution, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias and predictive power; 2024 work demonstrates benefits from correcting sampled rank estimates. These findings support candidate-count sensitivity probes, while preserving the host’s fixed 99-negative evaluator and macro validation HR@10 for selection. [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [rank estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371).

Embedding diagnostics should examine the singular-value spectrum alongside cosine similarity: ICML 2024 documents low-rank embedding collapse in recommendation models. Effective rank can summarize dimensional concentration, but should accompany behavioral measurements—full-catalog unseen-item top-list coverage, recommendation-frequency concentration and performance stratified by training-item frequency and history length. Geometry alone does not establish recommendation quality. [Embedding collapse](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html).

Suggested calibration protocol: freeze training-prefix probes and candidate draws; bootstrap paired per-user differences within each category, then recompute the four-category macro mean. User-level paired comparisons have established precedent in ranking-metric evaluation. Inject controlled defects into temporary diagnostic copies—incorrect left-padding readout, shuffled histories, collapsed embeddings or popularity-dominated scores—and measure which probes detect them. This fault-injection suite is a proposed engineering validation approach, not an established finding from the retrieved papers; history shuffling alone need not worsen a model that ignores order. Bootstrap intervals quantify user-sampling uncertainty, not repeated-search bias. Keep all auxiliary probes diagnostic-only and retain one trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category. [Ranking-metric assessment](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09377-x).
